title: Arbor POC - Cache Strategy Weekly Review
topics: Security: audit logs and KMS note
summary: Weekly POC sync to review cache hit-rate improvements, discuss prompt reuse strategy and templating to increase prefix hits, validate prefetch TTL adjustments, and agree on a short benchmark plan. Customer is aiming for 70-80% effective cache hit for common flows; current observed end-to-end token cost reduction ~12% but not meeting target. Action items: Redwood to share TTL/playbook and prefetch script; Arbor to run 24-48h synthetic with new prompt templates and share logs; next sync in one week.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share TTL tuning playbook and example prefetch script (2025-09-05)
Maya Patel: Export current prefix/KV cache hit-rate dashboard and raw sample of mismatched prompts (2025-09-04)
Priya Singh: Run 24h synthetic with normalized prompt templates and attach logs (2025-09-06)
Hiro Tanaka: Open support ticket with request for deeper KV cache metrics (trace-level) if hit rate doesn't improve (2025-09-07)
next_steps: Redwood will send a small TTL/playbook zip + prefetch script and a short README
Arbor will run synthetic run with prompt templates and report hit-rate change
If results < target, schedule 1h deep-dive with Redwood runtime engineers to look at kernel-level traces
transcript:
Header: 2025-09-02 14:00 PDT | Duration 42m | Recording ID ff-2025-09-02-arbor-cache-93a1
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Kaur (Redwood CSM), Elena Martinez (Arbor ML), Hiro Tanaka (Arbor SRE), Priya Singh (Arbor DS)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Elena: Elena here.
[00:06] Hiro: Hiro present.
[00:07] Priya: Priya here.
[00:08] Jordan: Awesome. Maya, want to kick off with the hit-rate numbers?
[00:13] Maya: Yeah, sure. So we ingested the week two telemetry and the gross numbers: global prefix cache hit is at about 48% on the UI, overall KV cache hit 56% — those are live metrics from the dev pool. There's a note that some of the counts are aggregated; we see a big delta between session-level prefix hits and token-level effective hits.
[00:34] Hiro: Wait, quick clar — when you say prefix hit is 48%, is that per-request or per-token? Our dashboards show something different.
[00:40] Maya: Good point. It's per request where the prefix matched — so requests that fully used a cached prefix. The per-token effective reduction is lower because prompt variability causes shortfall. So token-level savings are more like 12% net reduction in tokens generated.
[01:00] Elena: OK, that explains why our cost numbers didn't drop as much as we expected when we turned caching on. We were expecting closer to 30%.
[01:07] Jordan: Right. The common theme we've seen: templating and prompt normalization gives you much better prefix reuse. We recommended earlier to standardize variable placeholders rather than full free text.
[01:20] Priya: We tried that for the billing flow but didn't push it everywhere. A lot of the prompts still have user names, dates, micro-phrases.
[01:29] Maya: Exactly. Small differences — like 'Dr.' vs 'Doctor' or 'card ending in 1234' — will break prefix hits. We can do a normalization layer at the client or server side to canonicalize those fields.
[01:45] Hiro: Is there an easy mapping? I worry about latency added by normalization.
[01:49] Maya: It is cheap: regex replacement and simple templating. On our stack it's typically sub-ms. We can provide a library snippet.
[01:57] Jordan: We'll include a small JS/Python snippet in the playbook.
[02:03] Elena: Can we see examples of mismatched prompts that failed to hit? That would help our engs tune the templates.
[02:10] Maya: I'll export a sample of top-500 prompt variants that missed and send that — we spotted patterns: personalization tokens in different positions, optional clauses, and slight rewording.
[02:24] Priya: Great.
[02:26] Maya: Also, we did a quick experiment with prefetching for the appointment reminder flow; prefetch increased effective prefix hit to 68% for that specific flow, because we load the expected next-step context into KV ahead of time.
[02:39] Elena: Prefetch sounds promising but how do you choose what to prefetch? We don't want to over-cache.
[02:44] Maya: We recommend using your orchestration signals: user step, recent events, and TTL heuristics tuned to the flow frequency. In the playbook we'll include a heuristic table: high-frequency flows get longer TTL, low-frequency short TTL.
[02:58] Hiro: About TTLs — what did you change for the prefetch test?
[03:02] Maya: We bumped TTL from 30s to 2 minutes for that flow and used LRU eviction for the dev pool. It gave better hit rate, but of course it increased memory footprint.
[03:14] Hiro: Memory is OK in dev but in prod we have limits. We need numbers on memory vs hit-rate tradeoff.
[03:20] Jordan: We'll include an expected memory delta estimate in the playbook and a simple formula: expected_mem = avg_prefix_size * entries. We can also run a quick estimate against your sample traces if you give them to us.
[03:33] Priya: On the prompt reuse angle, we tried grouping prompts into buckets — basically light-weight templates — but our mapping is manual and feels brittle. Is there tooling to auto-suggest templates?
[03:45] Maya: We're working on a simple clustering script that uses tokenized n-gram similarity to propose canonical templates. We'll provide a beta script in the repo; you can run it on the logs. It's not perfect but helps reduce the manual.
[03:59] Elena: That would be super helpful.
[04:02] Jordan: Quick commercial note — if arbor wants Redwood to run a managed normalization pass on your logs as a service, we can scope that as a short engagement. But for now, the scripts should do.
[04:13] Elena: Let's try the scripts first.
[04:16] Maya: Cool. A few more items: we saw a regression in one key user flow — the triage flow — where prefix hit dropped to 32% this Wednesday. The likely cause: a prompt tweak in the app introduced a new optional sentence.
[04:30] Priya: That was me — I added clarifying text to reduce ambiguity in user responses. Didn't think about caching. Sorry.
[04:36] Priya: I can revert or we can template that clause.
[04:40] Maya: Templating is safer — revert can be risky. We'll show where to insert placeholders.
[04:47] Hiro: Any impacts to latency from these changes?
[04:50] Maya: Normalization + prefetch adds negligible cold-path latency; hot-path is unchanged. Prefetch can increase throughput by reducing downstream token generation load.
[05:02] Elena: Can we get a concrete target? We asked for 75% effective hit on our top 10 flows. Is that realistic?
[05:10] Maya: With templating and prefetching, 70-80% is realistic for deterministic flows. For highly variable free-text flows it's much lower.
[05:18] Jordan: We should prioritize top 10 flows first. If you get those to 75% you'll see the biggest dollar ROI.
[05:27] Priya: We'll prioritize.
[05:29] Maya: Another note: we discovered some mis-labelling in the telemetry — the UI shows 'KV hit' but it's actually combined k-v and prefix matches. We're going to send an updated dashboard CSV that separates prefix-only, kv-only, and combined hits.
[05:45] Hiro: Please do, because we need per-token numbers for our finance team.
[05:49] Maya: On security: you asked about audit logs and KMS. Nothing changed — the Private/ Dedicated options preserve logs to your S3 and keys through KMS. For the POC we store ephemeral logs in our demo bucket with access control.
[06:02] Elena: Is there any PII in these sample logs?
[06:05] Samir: We scrub sample logs — there may be hashed IDs but we mask any direct PII; we'll re-affirm the scrub process in writing.
[06:12] Priya: Thanks.
[06:14] Jordan: Back to the technical plan: Maya, can you walk through the benchmark plan for next week?
[06:19] Maya: Sure. Step 1: Redwood sends TTL/playbook + normalization scripts and prefetch sample (Tuesday). Step 2: Arbor runs a 24-48h synthetic replay of representative traffic with templated prompts and prefetch enabled for top flows. Step 3: produce report with: prefix-only hit, kv-only hit, combined hit, token reduction, memory delta. If combined hit < 65% we escalate to runtime deep-dive.
[06:48] Hiro: Who runs the replay — our infra or Redwood?
[06:51] Maya: Your infra to keep production parity. But we can provide the runner and help with setup.
[06:56] Elena: We'll run it ourselves and ask for help if needed.
[06:59] Priya: Quick question on instrumentation: what logs do you need to compute token-level savings?
[07:06] Maya: We need request payloads (hashed), response token counts, and cache match metadata (prefix_matched=true/false, kv_hits=n). We recommend a 1-in-10 sampling for full payloads and aggregates for everything else.
[07:20] Priya: OK we'll enable that sampling.
[07:22] Maya: One more gotcha — prompt shuffling in your client sometimes reorders optional clauses which breaks prefix keys. If you can standardize clause order in serialization that helps.
[07:34] Priya: Noted. We'll check our serialization layer.
[07:36] Elena: Any ask from our side on security/approval before we share logs?
[07:41] Samir: We'll send a short consent + scrub checklist. Please confirm you pass it and then share a secure bucket to drop logs.
[07:48] Elena: Will do.
[07:50] Jordan: OK let's do a quick timeline recap and owners.
[07:53] Jordan: Jordan to send TTL playbook and prefetch script by Friday (2025-09-05). Maya to export mismatch samples by Thursday (2025-09-04). Priya to run synthetic and share results by Saturday (2025-09-06). Hiro to open support ticket for trace-level metrics if needed by Monday (2025-09-07).
[08:15] Elena: Sounds good.
[08:17] Maya: Anything else?
[08:18] Priya: One last thing — are there quick UX changes we can do that won't break tests but help caching? For example rendering user name only at the end vs in prompt body?
[08:28] Maya: Yes, moving personalization to post-processing or placeholders is ideal. We'll add examples in the playbook.
[08:35] Jordan: Great. If no other items, we'll wrap. Next sync same time next week unless results prompt an earlier deep-dive.
[08:42] Elena: Thanks all.
[08:44] Jordan: Thanks, bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words removed for readability; there are minor ASR mis-hearings like 'KV cash' in one snippet but majority reviewed by CSM.
